title: Accelerated Activation: 8-Week Launch + 30/60/90 Continuum Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes an accelerated activation pathway designed for mid-market and developer-led customers that combines a high-touch 8-week onboarding sprint with a lighter 30/60/90-day continuation plan. The goal is to get a working integration, measurable value (first feature usage), and a renewal-ready adoption story within the first three months while minimizing time-to-value and operational overhead for CS.

When to use this playbook:
- New customers with clear pilot scopes (embedding/search, chat integration, moderation, or inference pipelines) where we expect measurable token/embedding volume within 8 weeks.
- Accounts with engineering engagement but limited resources for multi-month professional services.
- Renewal or expansion opportunities that need a fast time-to-first-success metric to accelerate expansion.

Primary success metrics (examples):
- Time to first meaningful inference call (TFFIC): target <= 10 business days
- Activation rate: 60% of seeded routes see > 10k tokens in 30 days post-launch
- Business KPI tied to integration (e.g., search CTR lift, automation throughput): measurable delta >= agreed baseline within 90 days
- Renewal likelihood signal: product usage in >2 core routes and NPS >= +20 at 90 days

Ownership and roles:
- CSM (Primary): Priya Nair — ownership of plan, weekly cadence, risk management
- Solutions Engineer (SE): Evan Chen — technical onboarding assist, runbook, triage
- Product/Support Liaison: Samantha Ortiz — escalate product bugs, track fixes
- Customer Technical Lead: named by customer — responsible for implementation tasks and PR reviews

High-level phases and milestones (8-week sprint):
Week 0 (Pre-kickoff):
- Deliverables: Welcome packet, success criteria worksheet, ephemeral API key instructions, architecture checklist
- Tasks for CSM: Confirm stakeholders, schedule kickoff, share playbook and folder links

Week 1 (Kickoff & Architecture):
- Kickoff meeting (45 min): objectives, success metrics, integration runway, security checklist, data flows
- SE: perform remote environment review; provide minimal viable integration template (MVI) repo link
- Customer tasks: provide API access scope, sample data, network info

Week 2 (MVI Implementation & Validation):
- Goal: Customer runs first end-to-end request against staging with basic example prompts
- SE: run pair-programming session (1–2 hours) if needed
- Deliverable: End-to-end smoke test report (pass/fail)

Week 3 (Feature Iteration & Observability):
- Add telemetry hooks (latency metrics, error rates, per-route token counters)
- Set up Redwood Console dashboards and alert thresholds
- CSM: schedule 1:1 adoption checkpoint

Week 4 (Quality & Performance Tuning):
- Implement caching/batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize quick audit
- Evaluate quantization or model variant recommendations if cost vs latency tradeoff present
- Deliverable: Performance delta table (baseline vs tuned)

Week 5 (Pilot Traffic Ramp):
- Gradual ramp to pilot traffic (e.g., 10% -> 50% of planned queries)
- Monitor for regressions; confirm fallbacks work (model routing, region failover)
- CSM: update risk register with mitigation actions

Week 6 (Feature Lock & Training):
- Freeze integration contract for pilot scope
- Deliverables: Internal runbook for on-call, hand-off slides for product ops
- Customer enablement session: how to interpret logs, cost reports, and quality monitoring

Week 7 (Go-live & Measurement):
- Full pilot traffic target reached
- Collect primary usage metrics and initial business KPI signals
- CSM: prepare preliminary QBR one-pager for week 8 review

Week 8 (Sprint Review & Transition to 30/60/90 Continuum):
- Formal review meeting (CSM + SE + customer stakeholders)
- Deliverables: Activation dashboard snapshot, improvement backlog, renewal/expansion hypothesis
- Agree next steps and schedule 30/60/90 checkpoints

30/60/90 Continuation (lightweight, automation-first):
30-day (post-sprint) — Stabilize and Expand:
- Focus: fix highest-severity issues, optimize prompts and routes with Redwood Optimize suggestions
- Success check: 30-day activation metric (tokens per route, hourly consistency)
- Actions: Automatic weekly digest email from Redwood Console to stakeholders; CSM 30-day check-in (15–30 min)

60-day — Adoption Health and Value:
- Focus: tie usage to product/business outcomes; run small experiments (A/B for prompts, reranker thresholds)
- Success check: positive movement on pre-agreed business KPI; adoption across at least 2 teams/flows
- Actions: Prepare mini-QBR slide (less than 5 slides) for customer stakeholders; list of product asks and roadmap mapping

90-day — Renewal and Expansion Readiness:
- Focus: construct renewal narrative (what improved, ROI signals, risk areas)
- Success check: renewal recommendation (yes/no) with supporting metrics
- Actions: Draft renewal forecast, propose expansion pilots or Dedicated offering if unit economics justify it

Meeting cadences and templates:
- Weekly 30-min tactical call (Weeks 1–6) — agenda: blockers, risks, short-term plan, owner updates
- Biweekly 45-min stakeholder sync (Weeks 7–8) — agenda: usage trends, business KPIs, decision items
- 30/60/90 check-ins: 15–30 min each, focused on health metrics and renewal signals

Risk register (example entries):
- Risk: Customer cannot provision networking access in time -> Mitigation: SE to provide local mock and test harness; shift feature scope to non-networked flows
- Risk: High token cost discovered during ramp -> Mitigation: Apply caching strategy, model variant fallback, and cost alerts; evaluate Dedicated pricing if sustained
- Risk: Quality regression after tuning -> Mitigation: Keep prompt regression test suite and rollback plan in Redwood Console

Template: Sprint kickoff agenda (45 min):
1) Introductions and roles (5 min)
2) Success metrics & acceptance criteria (10 min)
3) Integration architecture and security questions (10 min)
4) MVI plan and timelines (10 min)
5) Risks, communication channels, next steps (10 min)

Template: 30-min weekly tactical agenda:
- Quick status (5 min)
- Blockers and escalations (10 min)
- SE tech note / troubleshooting (10 min)
- Action items and owners (5 min)

Customer-facing one-pager (to share at week 8):
- One-line summary of success ("Search relevance pilot increased CTR by X%")
- Key metrics snapshot (TFFIC, daily active routes, token volume, latency p95)
- Remaining risks and asks (1–2 bullets)
- Next steps and recommended expansion lanes

Lightweight QBR slide deck outline (3–5 slides):
1) Executive summary and recommendation
2) Activation metrics + product usage trends
3) Business outcome evidence and ROI signals
4) Blockers & asks (product or infra)
5) Renewal / expansion proposal and next steps

Automation and templates we push to customers:
- MVI Git repo with example connectors (HTTP + SDK examples)
- Pre-built Redwood Console dashboard templates for activation KPIs
- Prompt/regression test harness skeleton (unit tests for prompt outputs)
- Cost-aware policy checklist (suggested batch sizes, token caps, and alert thresholds)

Playbook triggers for escalation to Enterprise motion:
- Sustained predictably high volume where Dedicated pricing would reduce unit cost by >25%
- Compliance or networking needs that require Private deployment
- Multiple business units planning adoption across regions (requires platform onboarding assistance)

Notes and scribbles (for working copy):
- Consider a 4-week fast lane for developer eval accounts with lower SLAs but faster time-to-first-call
- Add a simple NPS pulse at day 30; correlate with usage to identify accounts at risk early
- Keep the SE pairing budget to 4 hours during Week 2 to reduce hand-hold time and cost

Appendix: Quick checklist for CSM before kickoff:
- Confirm stakeholders and fallback contacts
- Share playbook and MVI repo link
- Create project folder in drive and invite collaborators
- Pre-fill success criteria worksheet and share with customer

End of document.
